The graph $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the horizontal segment for $x\in [-4,-1],$ the sloped segment for $x\in (-1,0],$ and the sloped segment for $x\in [0,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-1,0].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle below the $x$-axis, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we subtract its area.

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot 3) \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =6-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
